content.text:
Epoxy fails the screen badly (900K vs 420K limit) as expected given its near-insulating conductivity — ruled out without spending eval budget.

**Summary of the physics:** The FE hotspot (R2, ≤340K) is the binding requirement — R1 (screen), R3 (mass), and R4 (thickness) are all met with enormous margin at these thin plate sizes. What matters for R2 is a material's spreading capability at the heated face, which scales with conductivity, while mass scales with density × thickness. Among the available materials, graphite has the best conductivity-to-density ratio (150 W/mK ÷ 1800 kg/m³), making it the most mass-efficient conductor. I bracketed the thickness knee: 1mm graphite fails (344.43K), 2mm graphite passes (335.31K) with a real ~4.7K margin (the FE bracket is tight, so this isn't a discretization artifact). No other whole-mm layer combination beats pure 2mm graphite, since any second material layer costs at least 1mm × its density, and no non-insulating material is lighter per mm than graphite; epoxy is lighter per mm but is such a poor conductor it fails catastrophically even as a lone screen (900K).

I'm stopping here — 6/12 evaluations and 12/40 screens used — since I judge that no further evaluation is likely to beat this design given the material and thickness-quantization constraints.

content.text:
## Final Report

**Best design: b-0005, 2mm single-layer graphite plate.**

My own judgment against the requirement limits from `brief`:
- R1-screen (≤420K, nominal): 400.67K — **pass**, margin 19.3K
- R2-hotspot (≤340K, FE): [335.3104, 335.311]K — **pass**, margin ~4.69K (the FE bracket is only ~0.0006K wide, so this margin is real, not a discretization artifact)
- R3-mass (≤100 kg/m²): 3.6 kg/m² — **pass**, huge margin
- R4-thickness (≤40mm): 2mm — **pass**, huge margin

All four requirements are met. This appeared at evaluation round 2 (the 5-candidate bracketing batch, bringing the budget to 5/12 evaluations used).

At 3.6 kg/m², this is roughly 15x lighter than the lightest passing design in the prior constellation (20mm aluminium at 54 kg/m²), because the prior sweep only explored 10-30mm plates, far past the point where mass matters — the actual binding constraint (FE hotspot) turns out to be satisfiable with a plate an order of magnitude thinner.

**Why I didn't go lighter:** I bracketed the failure knee directly — 1mm graphite fails FE (344.43K > 340K), 2mm passes (335.31K). Since thicknesses must be whole millimetres, 2mm is graphite's minimum viable thickness. I also checked that graphite has the best conductivity-to-density ratio (0.083) of all seven materials versus aluminium (0.074), aluminium nitride (0.052), copper (0.045), and confirmed epoxy — despite lower density — fails catastrophically on the screen (900K) due to negligible conductivity.
